after: ## The four functions and what each needs from the others
alt: Four panels, one per function. Marketing needs quality products on time from operations, a budget from finance and good service staff from HR. Operations needs sales forecasts, money for materials and trained staff. Finance needs revenue forecasts, cost information and wage costs. HR needs staffing plans, skill requirements and a pay and training budget.
caption: Every function relies on the other three.

alt: Six steps for any large decision: objective, marketing (demand and price), operations (capacity and quality), human resources (staff and skills), finance (affordability and return), then risk and reward. A chain beside it shows a decision is only as strong as its weakest link, such as operations capacity or cash.
caption: Work through every function: a decision is only as strong as its weakest link.

alt: Higher reward usually comes with higher risk. Risk appears in every function: lower demand, equipment failure, rising costs or cash shortages, and staff leaving. It is reduced by research, small-scale testing, cash reserves, several suppliers, training and cash flow forecasts.
caption: Every function carries risk; how much is acceptable depends on the business.

alt: Forecast profits of £9,000, £14,000, £16,000 and £17,000 over four years total £56,000, an average of £14,000 a year. On a £60,000 fit-out, ARR = 14,000 ÷ 60,000 × 100 = 23.3%.
caption: The second shop’s ARR is 23.3%, if the forecasts hold.

alt: The bank balance starts at £8,000, falls to £4,300 after month 1 (net −£3,700) and £3,600 after month 2 (net −£700), then rises to £4,200 in month 3 (net +£600). The month 2 low point leaves little room for a surprise cost.
caption: A profitable plan can still squeeze cash in the first months.

alt: The second-shop decision seen by each function: finance (ARR of 23.3% on forecasts, a £3,600 low balance), marketing (2,572 items a month to break even, about 86 a day), operations (oven capacity and consistent quality) and human resources (staff recruited and trained before opening).
caption: Each function reads the same figures for a different risk.

alt: The second shop costs £60,000, earns £56,000 over four years and has an ARR of 23.3%. The refit costs £20,000, earns £5,000 a year (£20,000 in total) and has an ARR of 25%. The refit has the higher ARR and lower risk; the second shop brings more total profit and growth.
caption: Higher ARR is not the whole story: objective and attitude to risk decide.

alt: An analysis chain coloured by function: promotion succeeds and demand rises (marketing), operations needs more stock, finance must pay suppliers before customers pay, so cash falls. A checklist reminds students to name a second function, use and interpret case figures and weigh reward against risk.
caption: Strong synoptic answers follow the effect from one function into others.
